narr: A cold front dropped down from the north, causing showers and thunderstorms to develop. The storm motion was nearly parallel to the boundary, causing some storms to train over the same area. This led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
ev: Beach Drive was shut down between MD-185 Connecticut Avenue and Kensington Parkway due to Rock Creek flowing out of its banks.
The service road of I-95/I-495 Capital Beltway Inner Loop was blocked by high water prior to US-1 Baltimore Avenue.
Several vehicles were stranded in high water due to Sligo Creek out of its banks near the intersection of MD-650 and Sligo Creek Parkway. Boats were deployed and New Hampshire Avenue was closed.

There was a rapid rise of several feet in about an hour along the Northwest Branch of the Anacostia River in Colesville. The water level crested above flood stage at 10.11 feet at 12:30 AM EST. The water level fell below flood stage at 1:45 AM EST. ||Backyards of homes on Kemps Mill Road just south of Randolph Street were flooded.
The water level rose rapidly over 6 feet in one hour, cresting at 10.71 feet at 12:45 AM EST. The Anacostia River Park around near 38th street began to flood.
MD-410 East-West highway was closed at MD-212 Riggs Road due to Sligo Creek being out of its banks.
Several homes with basements were flooded and families were displaced due to flooding.
A neighborhood was flooded near the intersection of 23rd Avenue and Sheridan Street. Multiple people were trapped or displaced.
The roadway from I-495 Capital Beltway to Clara Barton Parkway was blocked due to high water.
There was a rapid rise along the Northwest Branch of the Anacostia River at Brentwood around 7.2 feet in fifty minutes.
There was a rapid rise along the Northwest Branch of the Anacostia River at Brentwood of nearly six feet within an hour.
Th road was closed along little elk creek due to high water.
A few cars got stuck in high water along Calvert Road near North East Creek.
The road was closed due to flash flooding near the 300 Block of East Main Street.
A water rescue was reported on Wise Avenue.
A water rescue was reported on Route 40 in White Marsh due to high water.
A water rescue was reported along Honeygo Boulevard due to high water.

The water level along Whitemarsh Run rapidly reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.88 feet at 9:25 PM EST on the 2nd of July. The water level fell below flood stage at 10:55 PM EST. ||Water covered the parking lots near the stream, particularly near the Town Center Court.

The water level along Turkey Branch rapidly rose above flood stage, cresting at 10.5 feet. Water approached the intersection of Turkey Branch Parkway and Danvers Street, and the intersection of Turkey Branch Parkway and Grenhole.
MD-28 was closed between Avery and Baltimore Roads due to flowing water from Rock Creek.
A water rescue occurred along Village Lane and Rippling Brook Drive in about two feet of water.
A vehicle was stranded in high water at the intersection of Longmead Crossing Drive and Layhill Road.
About six inches of flowing water was across Dale Drive near Ellsworth Drive.
Three vehicles were stranded in high water along Sligo Creek as it overflowed its banks onto Sligo Creek Parkway near Schuyler Road.
